# Configure Boundary OIDC authentication with Okta

Boundary delegates authentication to [Okta](https://www.okta.com) using the [OIDC (OpenID Connect) auth method](/boundary/docs/domain-model/auth-methods#oidc-auth-method-attributes), a common single sign-on (SSO) integration. Registering Boundary as an Okta app integration takes two steps: configure the app integration in Okta, then create the matching OIDC auth method in Boundary.

## Prerequisites

- An Okta account. HashiCorp recommends using a test account that is not tied to another SSO method.
- Administrator access to Boundary.

## Create an Okta app integration

Registering Boundary as an app integration in Okta lets Okta authenticate Boundary users and redirect them back to Boundary after a successful login.

1. In the Okta Admin Dashboard, select **Applications**, and then select **Applications** again from the sidebar.
1. Select **Create App Integration**.
1. Select **OIDC - OpenID Connect** and **Web Application**, and then select **Next**.
1. Name the integration.
1. Under **Sign-in redirect URIs**, replace the default value with the following URL, replacing `BOUNDARY_ADDR` with the address of your Boundary controller:

   ```plaintext
   https://BOUNDARY_ADDR/v1/auth-methods/oidc:authenticate:callback
   ```

1. Set **Initiate login URI** to the same URL you used for the sign-in redirect URI.
1. Under **Sign-out redirect URIs**, add your Boundary address:

   ```plaintext
   https://BOUNDARY_ADDR
   ```

1. Under **Assignments**, select the users or groups that should be able to authenticate to Boundary, or select **Skip group assignment for now** and assign access later.
1. Select **Save**.
1. From the app integration's **General** tab, record the **Client ID** and **Client secret**. These map to the auth method's `client-id` and `client-secret` attributes.
1. Locate your Okta domain by selecting the account menu in the top-right corner of the page. The domain is listed beneath your username, for example `dev-12345678.okta.com`. This maps to the auth method's `issuer` attribute.

<Note>

Unlike some providers, the Okta `issuer` value must **not** have a trailing `/` at the end of the domain, for example `https://dev-12345678.okta.com`.

</Note>

## Create an OIDC auth method for Okta

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="UI" group="ui">

1. Log in to Boundary.
1. Select the scope in which you want to create the auth method.
1. Select **Auth Methods**, then select **New**.
1. Select **OIDC**, and complete the following fields:
   - **Name**: (Optional) An optional name for identification purposes.
   - **Description**: (Optional) An optional description of the auth method.
   - **Issuer**: (Required) Your Okta domain, without a trailing `/`.
   - **Client ID**: (Required) The app integration's **Client ID**.
   - **Client Secret**: (Required) The app integration's **Client secret**.
   - **API URL Prefix**: (Required) The address where your Boundary controller is reachable by Okta, for example `https://BOUNDARY_ADDR`.
1. Select **Save**.
1. Select **Edit Form**, scroll to **Signing Algorithms**, add `RS256`, and select **Add**.
1. Select **Save**.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

```shell-session
$ boundary auth-methods create oidc \
  -issuer "https://YOUR_OKTA_DOMAIN.okta.com" \
  -client-id "$CLIENT_ID" \
  -client-secret "$CLIENT_SECRET" \
  -signing-algorithm RS256 \
  -api-url-prefix "https://BOUNDARY_ADDR" \
  -name "okta"
```

The `issuer`, `client-id`, and `client-secret` values come from the Okta app integration settings. The `api-url-prefix` must match the address where your Boundary controller is reachable by Okta.

Refer to the [auth-methods create](/boundary/docs/commands/auth-methods/create) command documentation for additional fields that you can use when you create OIDC auth methods.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Terraform" group="terraform">

Apply the following Terraform configuration:

```hcl
resource "boundary_auth_method_oidc" "provider" {
  name               = "Okta"
  description        = "OIDC auth method for Okta"
  scope_id           = "global"
  issuer             = "https://YOUR_OKTA_DOMAIN.okta.com"
  client_id          = "CLIENT_ID"
  client_secret      = "CLIENT_SECRET"
  signing_algorithms = ["RS256"]
  api_url_prefix     = "https://BOUNDARY_ADDR"
}
```

Replace `scope_id`, `issuer`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, and `api_url_prefix` with the values for your scope and Okta app integration.

Refer to the [boundary_auth_method_oidc](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/boundary/latest/docs/resources/auth_method_oidc) resource documentation for additional fields that you can use when you create OIDC auth methods.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Troubleshooting

#### `oidc: issuer did not match the issuer returned by provider`

If you add a trailing `/` to the Okta domain, activating the auth method fails with an error similar to the following:

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```plaintext
oidc: issuer did not match the issuer returned by provider, expected "https://YOUR_OKTA_DOMAIN.okta.com" got "https://YOUR_OKTA_DOMAIN.okta.com/"
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

Update the auth method's `issuer` attribute to remove the trailing `/`, and try again.

## More information

- Refer to the [Auth method](/boundary/docs/domain-model/auth-methods#oidc-auth-method-attributes) domain model topic for the full list of OIDC auth method attributes.
- Refer to [Filter managed groups](/boundary/docs/rbac/users/managed-groups) to assign roles to Okta users based on claims returned by Okta, such as group membership.
- Refer to the [Okta documentation](https://help.okta.com) for information about configuring app integrations and custom authorization server claims.
